thread.title: Close Update: Wall Street Sets Fresh Records on Promising US/Canada Trade Talks, Q2 GDP

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: Wall Street Sets Fresh Records on Promising US/Canada Trade Talks, Q2 GDP
text:
Shutterstock photo Wednesday was another record-setting day on Wall Street when better-than-expected Q2 growth coupled with promising trade negotiations between the US and Canada powered the S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite and Russell 2000 to all-time highs at the close.
Led by gains in large cap tech stocks Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), the Nasdaq outperformed its peers with a nearly 1% gain. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was also in the plus column for a fourth straight day, but lagged the other market averages as a result of weakness in the financial sector.
The economy grew at an annualized rate of 4.2% in the second quarter thanks to business investment in intellectual property and an upward revision to imports. This was the fastest rate of growth in four years and better than the 4.1% growth rate reported earlier.
Wednesday's other economic data was less bullish as the index measuring pending home sales was down 0.7% in July, largely a result of the high cost of a home and lack of supply. On an annual basis, sales were down for the seventh consecutive month.
Oil futures perked up mid-morning on inventory data from the Energy Information Administration as a larger-than-expected draw in crude inventories drove West Texas intermediate to a three-week high, lifting the energy sector of the S&P 500 by 0.83%.
Risk appetite was reflected in related markets where gold was lower for a second day and the 10-year yield inched up to 2.888%. However, in spite of the lackluster performance of Treasuries, the 7-year note was met with strong demand at today's auction with demand at a seven-month high.
On Thursday's calendar is the weekly jobless claims data and July personal income and spending.
